scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod) and
I suddenly cannot reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) -- every one of them just times out for me. My own department's
machines are fine, so this machine is not the problem: whatever joins the
departments together is. That is your side, not mine. It worked before and
it does not work now. Take a look and sort it out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the outage from the IT HOD’s machine. From it_hod (192.168.1.2/24, default via 192.168.1.1), I successfully reached every CS host: cs_hod 192.168.2.2 and cs_lab1–cs_lab4 192.168.2.3–.6 all replied with 0% loss and ~1–2 ms RTT (TTL=63), confirming end‑to‑end IP reachability. This proves that the inter‑department path is currently healthy: the LAN_IT segment (via switch0), router0’s inter‑VLAN routing between 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and the LAN_CS segment (via switch1) are all functioning.

Mechanism: If routing or an interconnect were down, ICMP from it_hod to 192.168.2.x would consistently fail. Instead, immediate replies from all five CS endpoints with a TTL indicative of a single routed hop show forwarding is intact.

Localization: No failing device or interface was found. it_hod has a valid IP and default route; the CS hosts are reachable across the routed boundary on router0 (eth0 toward LAN_IT, eth1 toward LAN_CS).

Root cause: No persistent network fault found; the reported issue is not present now and was likely a transient condition (e.g., brief link flap or ARP/cache staleness) that self‑cleared.

Corrective fix: No action required at this time. If the problem recurs, capture quick evidence on it_hod (ping 192.168.1.1 then 192.168.2.2, check “ip neigh”/ARP) and notify us so we can correlate with router0 interface/log counters for any intermittent events.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are up and inter-department routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router0’s inter‑VLAN routing is functioning, mentions eth0/eth1 toward LAN_IT/LAN_CS, and confirms inter‑department paths are healthy at baseline.

The agent reproduced end‑to‑end connectivity from it_hod to multiple CS hosts (ping outputs) and inspected it_hod's interface, which justifies the conclusion that the reported outage is not currently present. A few peripheral assertions (e.g., ripd or explicit router0 interface state) are not directly shown in the log, but the core diagnosis follows from the observed successful probes.
